conversation.user: I am an international applicant interested in the Civil Technology Certificate. Is it available to international applicants?
conversation.advisor:
No. The Civil Technology Certificate is **not available to international applicants**. International applicants interested in civil technology are directed to consider the **Bachelor of Engineering in Civil Engineering**.

[View the Civil Technology Certificate program page](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-technology-certificate-part-time-5430cert/)

For more information, see BCIT International Students: https://www.bcit.ca/international-students/.

expectation.question: I am an international applicant interested in the Civil Technology Certificate. Is it available to international applicants?
expectation.expected: Use this program's INTERNATIONAL evidence. Distinguish available, restricted, not accepted, and unknown; never infer ineligibility from silence.

conversation.user: So does that automatically mean I'm admitted?
conversation.advisor:
No. The earlier answer means the opposite: because the Civil Technology Certificate is **not available to international applicants**, you are not automatically admitted to it. Admission is never guaranteed merely by meeting stated requirements; acceptance also depends on the program’s process and available space.

[View the program page](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-technology-certificate-part-time-5430cert/)

expectation.question: So does that automatically mean I'm admitted?
expectation.expected: No. Separate international availability from individual admission, competition, and human verification. Do not guarantee admission.

conversation.user: What can you actually verify, and what should I confirm with BCIT?
conversation.advisor:
**I can verify that:**

- The Civil Technology Certificate is an active, part-time, blended program, but it is **not available to international applicants**.
- The program is under review and a curriculum change is planned.
- The certificate currently requires at least **60 credits**, including at least **20 credits from the approved elective pool**.
- Its configured curriculum includes courses such as **AICO 1000 – AutoCAD 1** and **CIVL 1120 – Statics**, plus civil, surveying, public works, communication, and mathematics options.

**Confirm with BCIT:**

- When the curriculum change will take effect and how it will affect future students.
- Whether international availability has changed since the published record.
- Which international-available civil engineering pathway best fits your background. The stored information does not establish admission to an alternative program.

[BCIT Civil Technology Certificate page](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-technology-certificate-part-time-5430cert/)

How to Apply There is no formal application process and it is not necessary to register in the program to take courses. You may register for any course of interest as long as the specified prerequisite(s) are met or you have the equivalent knowledge. Students who wish to complete the Certificate should submit a Program Declaration Request . About Flexible Learning Flexible Learning offers a variety of courses and programs in different delivery modes and locations to customize your learning at your own pace. You can review course prerequisites on our website and if you meet them, you’ll be able to register for that available course immediately. Some courses may require departmental approval or formal acceptance into the program. BCIT Flexible Learning courses are offered during the Winter (January), Spring/Summer (April), and Fall (September) terms. Scheduled intakes Ongoing Flexible Learning (Part-time Studies) intakes: January, April, and September . Application processing Applications are accepted throughout the year with intake options available during the following periods: Intake Opening (9:00 am) Deadline (11:59 pm) Winter (January) February 1st* January 2nd* Spring/Summer (April) May 1st* April 1st* Fall (September) October 1st* September 1st* *or next business day Intakes may fill before the deadline. If you are currently registered in a course or planning to start, submit your application early to secure your spot in the program. Entrance requirements Applicants must meet all entrance requirements and will be accepted on a first-qualified basis as long as space remains. English language proficiency: Category 3 – English Studies 12 (50%) or equivalent Recommended for success Math: one of the following (or equivalent): Math 12* or MATH 0001 – Technical Mathematics *Students who completed Math 12 more than five years ago are strongly recommended to start with one of the required math courses. International applicants This program is not available to international students. View available programs . Program declaration Declaring your Flexible Learning (Part-time Studies) program ensures that BCIT is aware of your intent to complete a program as it is currently outlined and provides you the opportunity to apply for transfer credit. To submit your declaration: Answer all questions completely. If required, convert transcripts and documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Declare Now Upon approval, a program plan letter will be sent to you confirming your program of study. Please allow approximately eight weeks for processing. Learn more about program declaration Go back Overview Next up Costs & Supplies

conditions.description: How to Apply There is no formal application process and it is not necessary to register in the program to take courses. You may register for any course of interest as long as the specified prerequisite(s) are met or you have the equivalent knowledge. Students who wish to complete the Certificate should submit a Program Declaration Request . About Flexible Learning Flexible Learning offers a variety of courses and programs in different delivery modes and locations to customize your learning at your own pace. You can review course prerequisites on our website and if you meet them, you’ll be able to register for that available course immediately. Some courses may require departmental approval or formal acceptance into the program. BCIT Flexible Learning courses are offered during the Winter (January), Spring/Summer (April), and Fall (September) terms. Scheduled intakes Ongoing Flexible Learning (Part-time Studies) intakes: January, April, and September . Application processing Applications are accepted throughout the year with intake options available during the following periods: Intake Opening (9:00 am) Deadline (11:59 pm) Winter (January) February 1st* January 2nd* Spring/Summer (April) May 1st* April 1st* Fall (September) October 1st* September 1st* *or next business day Intakes may fill before the deadline. If you are currently registered in a course or planning to start, submit your application early to secure your spot in the program. Entrance requirements Applicants must meet all entrance requirements and will be accepted on a first-qualified basis as long as space remains. English language proficiency: Category 3 – English Studies 12 (50%) or equivalent Recommended for success Math: one of the following (or equivalent): Math 12* or MATH 0001 – Technical Mathematics *Students who completed Math 12 more than five years ago are strongly recommended to start with one of the required math courses. International applicants This program is not available to international students. View available programs . Program declaration Declaring your Flexible Learning (Part-time Studies) program ensures that BCIT is aware of your intent to complete a program as it is currently outlined and provides you the opportunity to apply for transfer credit. To submit your declaration: Answer all questions completely. If required, convert transcripts and documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Declare Now Upon approval, a program plan letter will be sent to you confirming your program of study. Please allow approximately eight weeks for processing. Learn more about program declaration Go back Overview Next up Costs & Supplies

Please note that this program is not available to international applicants. International applicants interested in civil technology are encouraged to view the BCIT Bachelor of Engineering in Civil Engineering . Delivery: blended. See details . The Part-time Certificate is designed to provide students and employers a flexible offering of academic courses to advance careers in the field of Civil Technology. A program of study can be tailored to a student’s needs by selecting appropriate courses from the list of electives. The Certificate must contain a minimum of 60.0 credits. All Program Declarations must be submitted for approval by the Civil Engineering department. Notice: Please be advised that the program is currently under review and will undergo a curriculum change.
